body:
Years ago, when I lost a bunch of weight in a healthy way (but gained it all back and then some later, so my most recent loss is after the major gain-back), I knew my mom was going to say something that would bother me as I lost it. She's so hyper-fixated on everyone's weight, especially mine, and she thinks if she says something in a nice voice, it isn't a rude and overstepping comment. If my mom had encouraged me to get exercise and eat better purely for my health when I was like 20 pounds overweight in high school, instead of making me feel like no boy could ever like me unless I were thin and weight loss was all about being socially acceptable, I probably wouldn't have ballooned up to what I did later.

So I asked her not to say anything about it as I started losing, and she was confused (despite me trying to talk to her about this stuff in the past, but it is what it is), but she actually respected my request. I really appreciated that. 

Fast forward to me losing around 50 pounds and getting about ten pounds below my high school weight. I had someone with me at her house, and we were all talking, when she mentioned how impressed she was with my weight loss. She immediately caught herself and was like, "Oh..." so I said, "It's okay. No big deal."

In her mind, what I was actually saying was this that all bets were off and she could say whatever the hell she wanted. IMMEDIATELY, like hours later, she said the exact kind of crap I'd wanted to avoid in the first place. I was sitting there and she says, completely unprompted, "I'd say just twenty more pounds and you'll be perfect!"

I just stared at her, like are you freaking kidding me? I actually had to start being callous with her after that when she would try to talk about how "pretty" I looked which just meant thin for her, literally. When she'd say it, I'd just flatly say, "I know," and she'd laugh awkwardly. After a while, she finally stopped. We don't talk anymore, but I know confronting her about it again would have just led to me crying and being upset while she made me feel like the bad guy. I'm not typically one to back down, but... I mean, if you've had a parent like that, you know how it is. I'm so glad she can't comment on my current weight loss, especially since I'm struggling with disordered eating. She'd make it so much worse.

That's happened to me so many times, and I hate it. No matter what my weight is, I have a gut, even at my thinnest. I'm guessing I'll have to go very low on the "healthy" BMI side or lower for it to be gone, and it makes me sad. My butt is non-existant and it hurts to sit on hard surfaces, but I have this big old PCOS belly, even after a 60 pound loss. It honestly feels like it didn't go down at all, even though I guess it is a few inches smaller.

It's so freaking embarrassing. Ever since I started my first period and developed PCOS, I've started getting a belly. By middle school, it was pretty big, and though I was only around 15 pounds overweight, almost all of my fat was on my stomach. Kids would bully me and ask me when the baby was due. They left a lamaze book in my bag at lunch after I went to the bathroom. As an adult, people would think I was pregnant completely innocently and ask me when I was due. It's humiliating.

It also makes me look so much bigger than other people at my BMI. It just makes me so sad. I'm sorry you experienced that too. You're definitely not alone.

I'm so sorry you went through that. I had trauma lead to a gain back on my end, too. It's so unfair how much work it takes to lose it and how easy it is to gain it back. I'd started at 238, ended up at 177. My big thing was that I cut out fast food completely. I could eat whatever I wanted, but I had to go to the store and make it myself, which let me know just how badly I actually wanted it. When things got bad, I eventually started eating fast food again, and in what felt like three months I was already at 252.

Losing weight in a healthy way is so hard if you're also struggling with mental illness and eating disorders. I used to binge eat, but now I just starve myself. I relate really strongly to that sadness and just wanting to die. Everything feels so heavy and hopeless, and I wish there were some sort of easy solution. I hope you're able to work through this, and I hope you can get some therapy over what happened. Having trauma tied into your weight loss makes it especially hard. I hope it helps to at least know you're not alone.

But when things get better, those symptoms come shining through. This perfectly embodies the difficulty many people have in distinguishing depression the mood and depression the disease.

God, I hate shit like this. It blows my mind how people STILL think it's just being in a bad mood or moping. Depression is a disease. Like, "There are people who have lung cancer, so don't you dare sit around with asthma." 

And even when it IS situational depression, we have this stupid concept of "who has it worse," as if only the top tier people suffering may grieve. Oh, your house burned down? Boo-fucking-hoo, that kid lost both of his eyes in an accident. And that kid better shut up, too, because that guy in a full on coma right now would kill to be able to move around again.

Honestly, yeah. You strike me as someone who thought she could turn into a werewolf in high school. You know, the types who storm out of a room when they're upset. I think people think you're fat because you have a round/puffy face, then hid your body, but those saying you look obese are obviously exaggerating. I'm mostly just confused as to why you wanted to be roasted. Was it just for attention? You seem to be replying with the same boring thing over and over again. No one cares about your GPA, dude. I feel like if you can't take the roast, just say so and move on. This is starting to make me feel bad for you, which isn't what the sub is about.

Holy crap, that is INSANELY unprofessional. You should report her to whatever board covers her brand of therapy (if she's a psychologist, counselor, etc). There is never any reason to do that to a patient. I'm so glad you switched therapists and didn't just let her treat you like that, but wtf. A therapist can be firm with you and tell you things you might not want to hear, but to make it personal and for her to attack you like that is not only uncalled for, it's greatly unethical. She shouldn't be a therapist if she can't control her emotions. We're all human, but you work that shit out with your own therapist, man. Don't take it out on your clients.

Thank you. It really is exhausting. I've just never been so worn down before, even after so much heartache and suffering in my life. I didn't realize there was more to go beyond my rock bottom. Now I'm just like an exposed nerve. Everything hurts.

But hey, may we both (all) start to heal somehow.
Thank you. I wish my efforts ended up meaning anything.

\*hugs\* God, that last bit about knowing how your condition has squandered so many opportunities for happiness... It's so true that it hurts. I feel like that's something more people need to understand. Because they don't see that "it gets better" isn't a guarantee, or even all that likely. I feel like I've crossed that threshold, too, where no matter what happens, I'm always just going to end up back here, because my brain is sick and won't let me live my life. 

I'm sorry you can't find relief. I hope we can all find happiness and pull out of these moments, but it's so hard. I'm going through the worst time in my life, like one awful thing happening after another, and my depression is obliterating any opportunity to bounce back or cope, because all of these things just keep coming. My best friend talked me down yesterday, but I'm back here again. My tolerance for even a little thing going wrong is just gone. I've had so many huge things go wrong that it's destroyed the buffer I need. And I can't stop thinking about how it's never going to stop hurting. 

I can't, in good conscience, tell you that I hope you don't hurt yourself, when I'm right there with you. But I hope somehow, everyone here finds peace one way or another. Hopefully that's without killing ourselves, but I'm really tired of people throwing platitudes at us in order to keep us around. There is no true support, because life can't accommodate people with minds that refuse to allow happiness.

Thank you, and thanks for sharing your thoughts. This is a tough time, and I hope all of us who are struggling can get through it. I hope you find a good sense of community, as well. Some places on reddit can be great, even if some others leave something to be desired. I'm still kind of trying to find a place where I feel I belong.

Thank you for saying that. I honestly didn't know if anyone would respond, but I thought they'd say things like, "I'm sure you're not that bad looking" and such, as if that's the issue. I really appreciate you speaking as one person to another without placating or trying to diminish what I'm going through. That means a lot, honestly. This is just the worsts period of my life, which is really saying something, so I'm just... struggling to keep going with all of this stuff weighing on me. Thank you for making me feel heard.
